facts.fact: Customer support helps users resolve issues and achieve their goals with a product
First response time (FRT) measures how quickly a customer gets an initial reply
Mean time to resolution (MTTR) measures how long it takes to fully resolve an issue
Customer satisfaction (CSAT) surveys measure happiness after each interaction
Net Promoter Score (NPS) measures how likely customers are to recommend the product
Tickets are individual support requests tracked from creation to resolution
Triage categorizes and prioritizes incoming tickets by urgency and impact
SLAs (Service Level Agreements) define response and resolution time commitments
Escalation routes complex issues to specialized teams when frontline can't resolve
Knowledge bases provide self-service answers to common questions
Canned responses save time on frequent questions but must be personalized
Active listening means understanding the customer's actual problem, not just their words
Empathy statements acknowledge the customer's frustration before jumping to solutions
Root cause analysis finds the underlying issue, not just the symptom
Reproducing the issue is the fastest path to understanding and fixing it
Clear communication: explain what you're doing, why, and what to expect next
Follow-up after resolution confirms the fix worked and the customer is satisfied
Bug reports from support must include steps to reproduce, expected vs actual behavior, and environment
Feature requests should capture the use case, not just the requested feature
Support metrics inform product improvements — track common issues and pain points
Zendesk is a leading customer service platform with ticketing, chat, and knowledge base
Intercom provides in-app messaging, bots, and customer data platform
Freshdesk offers ticketing, automation, and multi-channel support
Help Scout provides email-based support with a focus on personal conversation
Slack Connect enables shared channels with customers for real-time support
Discord communities provide peer support and direct company interaction
Jira Service Management integrates support with development workflows
Automation rules trigger actions based on ticket conditions (routing, tagging, responses)
Macros apply pre-defined sets of actions to tickets with one click
Triggers fire automatically when tickets are created or updated
Views organize tickets into work queues by status, assignee, or condition
Tags label tickets for reporting, routing, and automation
Custom fields capture product-specific information on tickets
Satisfaction surveys automatically send after ticket resolution
Reporting dashboards track volume, response time, resolution time, and satisfaction
Chatbots handle common questions and route complex issues to humans
Screen sharing tools (Loom, CloudApp) help demonstrate solutions visually
Internal notes communicate between agents without the customer seeing
Side conversations loop in other teams without creating new tickets
API integrations connect support tools with CRM, analytics, and engineering systems
Greet the customer warmly and thank them for reaching out
Restate the problem in your own words to confirm understanding
Set expectations: tell them what you'll do and how long it might take
Use plain language — avoid jargon unless you know the customer is technical
Be specific: 'I've updated your account settings' not 'The issue has been resolved'
Provide step-by-step instructions with screenshots when possible
Offer alternatives: if the ideal solution isn't available, suggest workarounds
Admit when you don't know — 'Let me check with the engineering team and get back to you'
Never blame the customer — even if they made an error, focus on the solution
De-escalation: stay calm, acknowledge feelings, focus on what you can do
Positive language: 'The feature will be available next month' not 'We don't have that yet'
Close with a summary of what was done and an invitation to reach out again
Tone matching: mirror the customer's formality level while staying professional
Cultural awareness: communication norms vary across regions and languages
Written communication lacks tone of voice — use emoji and formatting carefully to convey warmth
Handle multiple customers simultaneously without making any feel neglected
Document solutions as you discover them — your future self and teammates will thank you
Ask clarifying questions: open-ended to explore, closed-ended to confirm
The 'five whys' technique traces a problem to its root cause
Celebrate wins: share positive feedback with the team to maintain morale
